subject: gk
question:
Public goods possess which of the following features in the economy?

I. They are non-rivalrous.

II. They are non-excludable.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Public goods are goods or services that are consumed by everyone in the society, regardless of whether they have paid for it or not.
 
• **Non-rivalrous means that one person's consumption of the good does not reduce the amount available for others.**
 
• For example, if a park is a **public good,** one person's enjoyment of the park does not prevent others from enjoying it as well.
 
• **Non-excludable means that it is difficult or impossible to prevent someone from consuming the good, even if they have not paid for it.**
 
• For example, it is difficult to prevent someone from enjoying the view of a fireworks display from a public space, even if they have not paid for a ticket to attend the event.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Private goods are goods or services that are consumed by individuals who have paid for them.
 
• **Private goods** **are both** **rivalrous and excludable.**
 
• **Common goods are goods or services that are available to everyone in the society but are rivalrous.**
 
• For example,** fish in a lake **can be a common good because if one person catches a fish, there is one less fish available for others to catch.
 
• **Club goods are goods or services that are non-rivalrous but excludable.**
 
• For example, a subscription to a streaming service is a club good because multiple people can consume the service at the same time without reducing the amount available for others, but only those who have paid for the subscription can access it.
